human_tolerance.notes: Reliance on human habitation 'has contributed to the species' proliferation, similar to rodents'. In urban and suburban areas it is typically seen in the cracks of old brick buildings, nests in trash piles, attics and under baseboards, and comes to outdoor lights to hunt moths.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: The breeding season runs from April to August, with eggs laid from mid-May to August in an average clutch of two. Males click to attract a mate and the female answers with her own squeaks.

phases.name: territorial
phases.note: Outside the breeding season, sheltering in cracks, walls and attics by day.

vocalizations.description: A distinctive high-pitched call 'somewhat like a squeak or the chirp of a bird', probably a territorial message; it also answers the click of a courting male.
The clicking a mature male produces to attract a female, answered by the female's own squeaks.

conservation.note: IUCN Red List category via Wikidata P141 (Q211005, least concern); the article adds that it 'holds no threatened or endangered status'.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Urban and suburban habitat, cracks of old brick buildings, nesting in trash piles and attics, attraction to outdoor lights and proliferation 'similar to rodents' are all from Wikipedia.

habitat.resources.note: Invertebrates from the diet; cavity and perch from where it shelters by day.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: A crack or cavity in a wall or building.

habitat.use.note: Shares authored: it is equally at home on walls and rock faces as on the ground.

look.note: Purple or tan skin with black spots, pale tubercles and white lower surfaces, a banded tail, large lidless eyes with elliptical pupils and a somewhat translucent belly; proportions and palette are authored.

range.note: Native countries are the Mediterranean-climate states listed in the article's Geographic distribution section ('Portugal, Spain, France, Italy, Greece, Israel, Malta, southern Bulgaria, North Macedonia, coastal Croatia ..., Bosnia and Herzegovina, the Adriatic islands, coastal Montenegro, the coastal part of Albania, Cyprus, Turkey, northern Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, Jordan, Syria, Libya, Egypt, Lebanon'); the wider spread into Africa, Asia and the Neotropics is described as introduction but is not enumerated, so only the United States and Mexico, which are named explicitly, are recorded as introduced.

seasonal.life_stages.note: It 'reaches sexual maturity within four months to a year'; the juvenile duration is authored from that.

seasonal.phases.note: The April to August breeding season, mid-May to August egg laying and the average clutch of two are from Wikipedia.

seasonal.strategy.note: No dormancy is described and it is established year-round in the southern United States; the strategy follows that.

traits.defense.note: Authored: withdraws into a crack or gap at the first disturbance, which is where it spends the day.

traits.diet.note: 'It is insectivorous' and it is 'a voracious predator of moths and small roaches', so the whole diet share is invertebrate.

traits.length_m.note: Midpoint of the 10-13 cm total length, which includes the tail; snout-vent length averages about 45 mm in males and 44 mm in females. The species 'rarely exceeds 15 cm'.

traits.lifespan_y.note: Maximum longevity of 7 years in males and 6 years in females from a wild population, determined by counting Lines of Arrested Growth.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: It walks over surfaces and climbs walls and ceilings on sticky toe pads; the two gaits are authored from that.

traits.mass_kg.note: Mean body mass 2.16 g in males and 1.97 g in females; 0.002 kg is the midpoint of the two means.

traits.mass_range_kg.note: 0.60-3.50 g in males and 1.02-3.11 g in females.

traits.nest_type.note: 'Their nests can be found in trash piles, attics, or under the baseboards of buildings.'

traits.social.note: Mature males hold small territories and call to keep others off; animals are otherwise seen one at a time.

traits.wariness.note: It lives inside the cracks and unseen areas of human homes and thrives on them; 0.1 is a judgement.

vocalizations.chirp.note: The high-pitched squeak or chirp used as a territorial message is from Wikipedia.

vocalizations.click.note: 'Male house geckos produce clicking sounds to attract a mate, with the females responding in their own squeaks.'
